web_evidence.title: Pearl S. Buck and the Forgotten Holocaust of Nanking
web_evidence.note: Scholarly analysis describes the novel's first, central, and final parts and reproduces interior base narration from widely separated pages; those passages externally narrate Ling Tan, his family, and other victims as he, she, and they, with access to their perceptions and no participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Why We Fight: Contending Narratives of World War II
web_evidence.note: Cambridge scholarly chapter analyzes Dragon Seed and quotes an interior passage that externally calls Ling Tan 'he' while reporting what he heard and understood, corroborating third-person narration.

search_log: Searched "Dragon Seed" "Pearl S. Buck" excerpt, first chapter, full text, and Ling Tan; located publisher, Google Books, Open Library, Internet Archive, and an unauthorized translated OCR result.

Searched "Dragon Seed" third person, narrator, point of view, omniscient, narrative, and focalization; no credible source explicitly used the grammatical label, but two scholarly sources supplied diagnostic interior prose and whole-book structural coverage.
Opened the Open Road Media publisher page and followed its Amazon and Google preview routes; Amazon failed and Google Play exposed only catalog copy, not sample prose.
Opened Google Books, Open Library, and Internet Archive records; Google Books remained snippet-only and the Internet Archive/Open Library edition required borrowing.

Opened and inspected the Review of International American Studies article and Cambridge University Press chapter; their quotations from separated interior scenes consistently corroborated third-person narration and revealed no alternating first- or second-person sections.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and narrates Ling Tan and other family members externally in third person, often entering their knowledge and perceptions. Quotes q00032 and q00051 independently expose that position; most first-, second-, and plural-person forms elsewhere are dialogue or universal maxims. Scholarly evidence covers the novel's major parts and quotes multiple separated interior scenes in the same third-person mode, while a second scholarly source independently corroborates it. No credible evidence of a sustained first- or second-person frame or alternating section was found; the only remaining limitation is that publisher and library previews were inaccessible as continuous authorized prose.
